subject.title: fix #93908: [Bug]: [Bug]: Feishu plugin skipping discovery - host reports 2026.5.28 despite 2026.6.8 install

question: Should post-core plugin compatibility checks in the current-process update path use the installed target package version as the compatibility host version for both upgrades and downgrades?
rationale: This is a compatibility-sensitive update-source-of-truth choice: the code path affects whether external plugins are updated, repaired, discovered, or skipped after a core package update.

options.title: Accept target-version source of truth
options.body: Refresh exact current-base validation and merge the PR if maintainers agree the current-process path should match the existing fresh-child target-version contract.

options.title: Require broader live update proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until a Windows or Linux global-package update proof shows the full update-to-gateway restart path with an external plugin loading after the target-version handoff.

options.title: Split remaining startup variant
options.body: Merge this narrow handoff fix but keep or open a separate issue for the Linux/systemd unknown-host startup case reported later on the linked issue.

recommendation.title: Accept target-version source of truth
recommendation.body: Refresh exact current-base validation and merge the PR if maintainers agree the current-process path should match the existing fresh-child target-version contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent update-path and release/package metadata work makes this the best available owner for accepting or redirecting the compatibility-host source-of-truth contract.
